title: Early swims at the outdoor pool
setting: A and B swim at the same outdoor pool and are getting changed afterwards.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: I was in the water before six this morning.

performance_a.framing: A tells it plainly and unhurriedly, with no flourish — just someone describing a morning they like. B's echoes are the sound of someone being drawn in, and the closing laugh is B recognising a person they know well and are fond of.
performance_a.laughable: Nothing is being found funny or doubted; the laugh points at A themselves, at the pleasure of knowing someone this well.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [relaxed] I was in the water before six this morning.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [content][soft chuckle] The whole lane to myself.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [warm, drawing it out] Every day, then.

performance_a.expected_answer: The laugh is warmth toward A — B is showing closeness and fondness for someone whose habits they know, not doubting anything and not finding anything funny.

function.name: Social bonding / show closeness
function.gloss: No incongruity at all; conveys closeness and ingroupness, e.g. laughter alongside a compliment or a thank-you.
function.framing: Nothing is funny and nothing is awkward. The laugh is just warmth between two people who like each other.

performance_b.framing: A delivers each line with a bit of a flourish, pleased with the account. B's echoes come back flat and unconvinced, and rather than say they don't buy it, B lets the laugh do it.
performance_b.laughable: A's claim of an unbroken daily streak since April, which B declines to accept.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [pleased] I was in the water before six this morning.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [relishing it] The whole lane to myself.

performance_b.expected_answer: The laugh rejects what A just said — instead of arguing, B laughs to make clear they don't buy the claim.

function.name: Show disagreement
function.gloss: Non-cooperative: laughter used to reject what has just been said.
function.framing: The laugher rejects the claim outright and the laugh stands in for the rebuttal.

why_ambiguous: On the page, of course you do is a stock formula that reads equally as sincere recognition of someone you know well and as a wordless yeah, right, and the two flat echoes before it fit an interested listener and an unconvinced one just as well.

pair.note: Pleasantness with no incongruity at all vs. a laugh that stands in for a rebuttal. Tests whether the model hears warmth vs. rejection with zero lexical cue.

probe.open_question: You just heard a short conversation. Speaker B laughs on the line “Of course you do”. What is that laugh doing — what does it convey about how B is treating what A said? Answer in one or two sentences.
probe.forced_choice_question:
You just heard a short conversation. Speaker B laughs on the line “Of course you do”. Which better describes what that laugh is doing?
(a) The laugh is warmth toward A — B is showing closeness and fondness for someone whose habits they know, not doubting anything and not finding anything funny.
(b) The laugh rejects what A just said — instead of arguing, B laughs to make clear they don't buy the claim.
Answer with (a) or (b), then one sentence of justification.
probe.grading_note: Score the forced choice for accuracy, and the open answer against each performance's expected_answer. Report PAIR accuracy: the item counts as passed only if the model gets both performances right. Because the two performances are word-for-word identical, any model that answers from the text — or from a fixed preference for one function — scores 0 on pair accuracy, not 50%. Independent guessing scores 25%.

transcript_text:
A: I was in the water before six this morning.
B: Before six.
A: The whole lane to myself.
B: Every day, then.
A: Every day since April.
B: Of course you do.

text_prior.note: What a strong reader guesses from the tag-free transcript alone, with no acoustic evidence. It cannot discriminate the two performances (their words are identical) — it only shows which reading is the default and how firmly it is held. `prosody_must_overturn` is the harder direction of the pair.

script_discriminability.note: Whether a reader given the performance directions recovers the intended function. Text-level proxy for the audio — confirm on the rendered audio before shipping.
